cim: Rubio faces G7 questions on Iran, Ukraine after GOP midterm losses
cim_eredeti: Rubio faces G7 questions on Iran, Ukraine after GOP midterm losses
szoveg_eredeti:
by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

PARIS (TNND) — Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Paris on Monday for talks with Group of Seven foreign ministers. Discussions are expected to include the Russia-Ukraine war, the conflict with Iran, energy security and artificial intelligence.

“We will focus on pushing for real accountability at the UN and advancing an innovation first agenda to secure the future of Super Intelligence,” Rubio wrote on X after landing.

The trip is Rubio’s first overseas visit since last week’s midterm elections, in which Republicans suffered heavy losses and lost control of Congress. Vice President JD Vance and President Donald Trump have cited the Iran war as a factor in the results.

The Paris talks also come amid protests in France, including in the capital.

Asked how U.S. allies are responding to the election results, Rubio said the countries he is meeting with this week understand the divisions in American politics.

“They, too, have experienced divisions in government and divisions in their own system,” he said.

Trump has proposed working with Europe to help end Russia’s war in Ukraine. His envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, are expected to meet with Ukrainian and Russian officials in the United Arab Emirates this week to discuss potential compromises.

Rubio said postwar security guarantees for Ukraine and Europe remain a key concern for U.S. allies. He told reporters in Florida before flying to Paris that some progress had been made on what those arrangements could look like.

“Nothing’s been finalized yet, and maybe some progress can be made in Abu Dhabi,” Rubio said.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Europe must be part of efforts to end the war.

“Europe must be part of the path to a solution” to the conflict, he said before traveling to Paris. “It is very clear that Europe doesn’t need a new security architecture, as Russia would have us believe, but simply the restoration of the existing security architecture.”

Qatar and other mediators, meanwhile, have proposed an interim solution to break a deadlock over the conflict with Iran. The conflict has driven up fuel prices and raised concerns about shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

Rubio said the sides are not “on the verge of a breakthrough,” while reiterating that Trump prefers a diplomatic solution. He said diplomacy has not been productive because Iran’s demands are “simply not just unacceptable.”

Rubio said he expects U.S. allies to have many questions about the conflict and what comes next.

_____Editor's note: The Associated Press contributed to this article.
